title: Badge rendering uses a nested double-IIFE where a plain computed const would do
description: The conditional badge in the collapsed header is built with an outer IIFE that contains an inner IIFE computing `badge`, then renders it. Every other derived flag in this component (richNodeDetail, showSourceOrigin, calculationBlockText, showCalculationHero, showSecondaryDetail, showColumnValuesTable, etc.) is a top-level `const` computed before the JSX. Hoisting the badge value to a `const badge = ...` above the return (matching the existing style) and rendering `{badge ? … : null}` removes one layer of IIFE nesting and aligns with the file's established pattern.
evidence: StepCard.tsx:165 `{(() => { const badge = (() => { … })(); return badge ? (…) : null })()}` — two nested arrow IIFEs inside JSX, vs. the const-flag pattern used at lines 88-122.
behavior_preservation: Pure refactor: the computed badge value and rendered output are unchanged; only the boilerplate that computes/returns it moves out of the JSX.
